title: KV cache + attention kernel edge-case debugging (scratchpad)
content:
Notes to self — quick playground + incident breadcrumbs

Context:
- Reproducing a production incident where per-token latency spikes and KV cache hit ratio drops to ~0 for a subset of requests. Customer traffic pattern: mix of short prompts (~64) and long contexts (>=4096).
- Suspected interaction between attention kernel selection heuristics and KV cache handling when sequence lengths cross certain thresholds (esp around 4096, 8192).

Summary of observable symptoms:
1) Latency: p50 ~ 30ms normally, during incident p50 jumps to 120–250ms for affected requests; p99 spikes > 800ms.
2) KV cache hit ratio: telemetry shows certain requests have kv_cache_hit_ratio ~= 0 immediately after a batch that had long seq_len requests.
3) Kernel selection: runtime logs show fallback from optimized kernel (flash_attn_v2) -> generic_attention after switching to long sequence mode.
4) Memory pressure: minor bump in GPU memory but not OOM; instead performance regression.

Reproduction attempts (local / dev cluster):
- Model: rl-model-open-7b (same arch as production test), compiled with kernel variants: flash_attn_v2, nv_attn_opt, fallback_generic.
- CLI commands used (redwood-cli approximate):
  # run single request via dev endpoint
  redwood-cli infer --model rl-model-open-7b --prompt "x" --max-tokens 64 --seq-len 64 --profile > /tmp/profile_short.txt

  # run long context request
  redwood-cli infer --model rl-model-open-7b --prompt "<long-context>.." --max-tokens 1024 --seq-len 4096 --profile > /tmp/profile_long.txt

- Combined test: interleave short and long requests to reproduce mixed-batch behavior
  for i in {1..100}; do \
    if (( i % 10 == 0 )); then \
      redwood-cli infer --model rl-model-open-7b --prompt "LENGTH4096" --seq-len 4096 --max-tokens 32 --no-stream &\
    else\
      redwood-cli infer --model rl-model-open-7b --prompt "short" --seq-len 64 --max-tokens 16 --no-stream &\
    fi\
  done

Observed outputs / snippets:
- runtime logs around kernel selection (trimmed):
  [2026-02-26 14:12:03] select_kernel: model=rl-model-open-7b seq_len=4096 batch_tokens=81920 -> chosen=flash_attn_v2
  [2026-02-26 14:12:03] kv_cache: reuse_enabled=true session_id=abc123
  [2026-02-26 14:12:03] batch_executor: merged 7 requests (short:6 long:1) total_tokens=86016
  [2026-02-26 14:12:03] select_kernel: model=rl-model-open-7b seq_len=64 batch_tokens=4480 -> chosen=fallback_generic (unexpected)
  [2026-02-26 14:12:03] kv_cache: evict_prefix session_id=abc123 evicted_bytes=124k reason=kernel-switch

- Profile snippets (from dev profiler):
  * When kernel=flash_attn_v2: per-token time ~0.9ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio ~0.98
  * When kernel=fallback_generic: per-token time ~3.5ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio ~0.02

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Kernel selection heuristic uses last-request seq_len to decide kernel for whole merged batch; if long request triggers flash_attn but then a subsequent short request batch gets evaluated separately but inherits a different kernel due to stale thread-local flag -> forced kv cache eviction.
B) There's a bug in prefix-KV metadata update: when attention kernel switches, we call kv_cache.invalidate_prefix(session) to avoid incompatible cache layout; that logic is too aggressive and doesn't check compatibility equivalence (e.g., quantized kernels share layout).
C) Some kernels (generic) use per-request memory layout that is incompatible with cached KV pointers; runtime conservatively evicts cache on kernel-change. Kernel-selection boundary based on batch_tokens > 65536 (heuristic) is too low for mixed traffic.
D) Edge-case: sequence-length exactly a multiple of 4096 or >8192 flips a compiled path which changes key/value dtype (fp16->bf16) due to a legacy optimization, causing mismatch and eviction.

Commands / queries to validate hypotheses:
- Search codepaths for kv_cache.invalidate_prefix and where kernel-switch triggers it:
  rg "invalidate_prefix|evict_prefix|kv_cache.*evict" src/ -n
- Add verbose logging in select_kernel to dump (kernel, seq_len, batch_tokens, thread_local_flags, compatible_kv_layout)
- Run a focused test that forces kernel-switch without changing seq_len dtype to see if eviction still happens:
  # force kernel switch flag via env var
  RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=nv_attn_opt redwood-cli infer --model rl-model-open-7b --prompt "short" --seq-len 64 --profile

Quick patch experiment (local):
- Change kv_cache.invalidate_prefix to only evict if compatibility_check(session, new_kernel) == false. Stubbed compatibility_check to always true for flash_attn_v2 vs nv_attn_opt.
- Rebuilt, ran interleave test with 1000 requests -> preliminary: kv_cache_hit_ratio stayed >0.9; p50 latency normalized.
- Risk: leaving compatibility_check lax could cause silent correctness issues if kernels truly incompatible. Need deterministic compatibility test (compare layout, dtype, kv-shape, quantization params).

Logs & error examples captured:
- Unexpected fallback: "select_kernel: heuristic mismatch - falling back to generic for small seq after mixed batch"
- Eviction trace: "kv_cache: evict_prefix session_id=abc123 cause=kernel-switch new_kernel=fallback_generic prev_kernel=flash_attn_v2"
- Downstream: "decode: token generation slower than expected - underlying attention op is generic_attention"

Minimal repro steps to hand to infra/SRE:
1) Start dev serving on node with single GPU (driver version X.Y.Z).
2) Load rl-model-open-7b with both kernels compiled.
3) Run interleave script (mix short=64/long=4096) at concurrency=8 for 2 minutes.
4) Watch /metrics: kv_cache_hit_ratio by session, kernel-selection events, and per-token_latency histogram.
5) Confirm whether a short request after a long request picks fallback_generic and triggers kv eviction.

Notes for fix design:
- Add compatibility matrix between kernels: kernel A <-> kernel B -> compatible? (based on dtype, kv layout, quantization flags).
- Avoid global/thread-local kernel flags that outlive a batch; scope kernel selection to the batch execution context only.
- If eviction required, record causation metadata (which field incompatible) for better telemetry.
- Consider adding a graceful hybrid path: keep KV cache but reformat lazily on first access by new kernel to avoid mass eviction.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there GPU driver/hw-level heuristics that cause a kernel to be unavailable at runtime (leading to fallback) and manifest as this behavior? (ask infra)
- Should we add a small deterministic test for exact power-of-two seq lengths (2048, 4096, 8192) to CI?
- Is there a model-compile-time flag that toggles layout change at 8192 token boundary? Search build scripts.

Next actions (short):
- [ ] Push compatibility_check prototype and run full test-suite (Marcus)
- [ ] Add verbose select_kernel logging for one canary host (Priya)
- [ ] Collect full profiler traces from production incident timeframe (Nina)
- [ ] Draft quick incident RCA once we confirm kernel-compatibility root cause

Random notes / heuristics observed while poking:
- Mixed short+long batching seems to produce non-intuitive batch_token counts that trigger thresholds. Consider using per-request kernel hints to avoid cross-request side effects during batching.
- Some of the drop-to-zero kv_cache_hit_ratio happened in sessions that did many small requests interleaved with occasional long ones; suggests session-scoped state got invalidated rather than global.

Scratchpad ends — saving this to Drive before I lose it.

If I get time: write a small unit-test that simulates two kernels with fake layouts and ensure kv_cache compatibility logic preserves cache when safe.

-- Nina
